newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia's Lek, Krka set to rise.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia's Lek, Krka set to rise.

text.p: Slovenian pharmaceutical producers Lek and Krka are expected to continue their current roll due to encouraging results and strong investor demand, analysts said on Monday.
"Lek's share price could grow to 45,000 tolars ($299), because it is potentially a very profitable company," said Danilo Grasic, head of investment at Austrian bank Creditanstalt in Ljubljana.
Since it was listed in September 1996, issue A of drug company Lek has soared by over 140 percent, and risen 70 percent since January alone.
At the close of trade on Monday Lek stood at 34,200 tolars, up 1.8 percent from Friday's close.

"Because of very strong foreign demand in Lek's shares, the company has become the most interesting also for domestic investors," one trader said. "Foreigners believe Lek is still cheap compared to similar companies elsewhere in Europe."
But some analysts warned Lek's shares could fall if optimism on the market waned.
"It's just a matter of psychology when prices will turn downward. Lek's current price is not supported by its earnings," said Mateja Gubanec of bank A banka.
Lek's biggest rival Krka was listed on Monday on the over-the-counter market of the Ljubljana bourse.
Krka ended the day 8.4 percent down at 26,010 tolars, but still well above the 7,043 tolars at which the bulk of the shares were sold off at.
Traders forecast Krka would rise to 30,000 tolars in the next couple of days.

Market participants said they did not expect investors to start selling Lek shares in order to buy Krka as there was a lot of fresh foreign and domestic capital waiting to be placed in Slovenian shares.
"The Slovenian market is attractive for most global investors because of its political stability and developed economy," Creditanstalt's Grasic said.
Krka and Lek, which are among the 10 largest Slovenian companies according to turnover, both produce over-the- counter, prescription and license drugs.
Each has a market share of about 27 percent in Slovenia, well above that of other domestic and foreign pharmaceutical companies.
Lek posted a preliminary pre-tax profit for 1996 of three billion tolars ($20 million), up from 2.9 billion in 1995. Its sales rose four percent to 38 billion tolars.
Krka said it expected its 1996 net profit to be some 10 percent higher than the 2.9 billion tolars tolars posted in 1995, while sales rose provisionally to 46.9 billion tolars from 44.1 billion.

The blue chip SBI index has risen by about 40 percent since the beginning of the year. The index ended at a record high on Monday for the fourth consecutive day, climbing 0.76 percent to 1,655.35. ($ = 150.2 Slovenian Tolars)
